do_not_change.summary: Preserve the same-project, same-run composite resolution reference.
do_not_change.evidence: Both schemas and both generated migrations reference (project_id, run_id, id) for resolution_recommendation_id; the service resolves destinations through recommendationDestination(projectId, row.runId, id). D1 and live-Postgres tests reject cross-run destinations and prove deleting a run containing a valid same-run resolution graph succeeds.
do_not_change.impact: This is the database-level tenant/run boundary that keeps a resolution from preventing deletion of a different run.
do_not_change.recommendation: Keep this composite self-reference and service lookup scope if later review states or Actions add related links.

do_not_change.evidence: The contract requires a structurally valid timestamp without comparing it to wall-clock time. The service recognizes exact stored replay first, then requires a future timestamp only for a new transition. Regression coverage exercises both outcomes.
do_not_change.impact: This maintains retry idempotency without allowing a newly created expired snooze.
do_not_change.recommendation: Keep temporal validation in the transition service after exact-replay detection.

do_not_change.summary: Preserve fact-hash-gated atomic normalized graph writes.
do_not_change.evidence: Parent insertion is conditional on a running run, and every child selects only the parent matching the complete immutable fact hash within the provider-aware batch. D1 and live-Postgres evidence cover exact retry and drift isolation.
do_not_change.impact: This prevents a conflicting retry from appending sources, targets or steps to the winning graph.
do_not_change.recommendation: Retain the parent fact-hash predicates and atomic batch semantics when extending the graph.
